opening.argument: The discussion centers on a studio interview about applying blockchain to real-estate records and operations. The speakers describe tokenizing properties and legal instruments, while explaining that the technology could address an aging structure and index deeds in chronological order. References to fabricated documents, signatures and scammers identify a fraud mechanism the project aims to reduce; the stated objective is that “we want to cut down as much of it as possible.” The separate Uphold segment states a rewards rate and monthly participation conditions, while the description warns that cryptoassets are highly volatile and capital is at risk. Nothing in the available evidence connects that disclosed sponsorship to the deed-fraud examples or presents those warnings as instructions to commit fraud.

citations.quote: We're actually tokenizing every property in Bergen County, and we're tokenizing the legal instruments and indexing them per property.
we're trying to solve is indexing deeds properly so you could tell the chronological order of history
Obviously bad actors will find different ways to try to scam people, but the point is we want to cut down as much of it as possible
Terms Apply. Cryptoassets are highly volatile. Your capital is at risk.
